title: The Broken Monsoon
premise: Rosalind Hartwell, a salvage diver who has spent twelve years outrunning her past one nautical mile at a time, is hired to recover equipment from a wreck the navy officially denies exists. When the government survey team that preceded her vanishes without tracks or bodies, she finds their logs describing something buried in the trench: evidence of an illegal deep-sea weapons program and the names of officials who will kill to keep it there. As she leads a ragtag expedition to bring the missing team home, Rosalind must choose between the duty of silence that keeps her crew alive and the justice of exposure that could redeem her own buried crimes. In the end she surfaces with the truth, trades her invisibility for testimony, and learns that love—for a lost teammate and for the crew who refused to abandon her—is worth more than safety.
about_author: Juniper Amberdale is a former maritime archaeologist who spent six seasons on salvage crews in the Coral Sea before turning to fiction full-time. She writes adventure novels from a houseboat office, drawing on real dives and the quiet moral compromises of people who work beyond the reach of law.

chapters.title: Twelve Miles Down
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. She completes a routine salvage dive on a freighter wreck, establishing her competence, her isolation, and her habit of measuring life in miles. A navy patrol boat shadows her too closely. Emotional beat: restless unease—the sense that her invisibility is fraying.

chapters.title: The Contract Nobody Signed
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. A broker offers triple pay to recover 'survey equipment' from coordinates the charts mark as nothing. She recognizes the hand of her old mentor, Elias Vane, in the paperwork. Emotional beat: temptation wrestling with instinct; she signs because debt and curiosity outweigh fear.

chapters.title: Crew of Strangers
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Rosalind and deckhand Mateo Cruz. She assembles a small crew—Mateo, engineer Priya Nair, and medic Sam Okonkwo—each hiding something. Emotional beat: wary camaraderie forming among people who understand not asking questions.

chapters.title: Coordinates That Don't Exist
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. En route, Priya discovers the survey vessel's last transponder ping ends mid-broadcast, no distress call. The sea is empty where the team should be. Emotional beat: creeping dread; the ocean feels like it is keeping a secret.

chapters.title: Gear and No Tracks
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. They find the survey camp intact—generators running, coffee cold, personal effects untouched—and no footprints leading away. Rosalind realizes someone left in a hurry or was taken without struggle. Emotional beat: horror sharpening into resolve; this is now a rescue, not a job.

chapters.title: The Logbook
chapters.summary: Sam's POV. Sam decrypts the survey team's logbook: they found a submerged facility in the trench and records naming officials behind an illegal weapons program. The final entry warns 'they know we know.' Emotional beat: the weight of knowledge—justice and danger arriving in the same breath.

chapters.title: What the Navy Won't Discuss
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. A navy frigate arrives, politely ordering them off-site. Rosalind stalls, hides the logbook, and recognizes the officer aboard: Commander Hale, tied to the program's names. Emotional beat: cold clarity—staying invisible was never really an option.

chapters.title: Descent Briefing
chapters.summary: Mateo's POV. Rosalind tells the crew part of the truth and offers anyone a way out. None leave. They plan a dive to the facility using the survey team's submersible. Emotional beat: chosen loyalty; strangers becoming a family bound by shared risk.

chapters.title: The Trench Line
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. First dive toward the facility. Pressure, darkness, and a sonar shadow that moves against the current. They find the survey submersible wedged in a canyon, hull breached from the inside. Emotional beat: claustrophobic terror and grief.

chapters.title: Survivor
chapters.summary: Sam's POV. Inside the wrecked submersible they find Dr. Lena Marsh, the only surviving survey member, half-mad from nine days alone. She whispers that the others were taken 'up the mountain'—to the facility. Emotional beat: fragile hope rekindled by a witness who must be protected.

chapters.title: Hale's Offer
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Hale boards under flag of parley and offers Rosalind money, immunity, and erasure of her own criminal past if she surrenders the logbook and Marsh. He knows exactly who she used to be. Emotional beat: the past as leverage; love of self-preservation against duty to others.

chapters.title: Twelve Years of Miles
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, Rosalind's POV. Her history unfolds: the accident she caused, the name she buried, why she measures life in miles. She understands Hale's offer is tailored to her exact wound. Emotional beat: reckoning—she cannot buy back her soul twice.

chapters.title: Mutiny of Conscience
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. The crew votes on whether to take the offer. Mateo argues for the missing team; Priya argues survival; Sam refuses to abandon a patient. Rosalind casts the deciding word: they dive. Emotional beat: unity forged through disagreement; power of collective choice over command.

chapters.title: Into the Facility
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. They infiltrate the flooded facility through a maintenance lock. Its corridors hold the vanished survey team's gear—and signs they are alive, held as witnesses. Emotional beat: awe curdling into anger at what power built in the dark.

chapters.title: The Archive Room
chapters.summary: Lena Marsh's POV, recovered and lucid. She guides them to the archive: proof of the program, test results, casualty lists—including civilians. Rosalind copies everything. Emotional beat: righteous fury; justice crystallizing into a plan rather than a feeling.

chapters.title: Taken
chapters.summary: Mateo's POV. Hale's men storm the facility. In the chaos, Mateo is captured covering the others' escape, and the archive copy is nearly lost. Emotional beat: sacrifice and guilt; the cost of the mission becomes personal and immediate.

chapters.title: Time Is Already Running Out
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. The facility begins a controlled scuttle—evidence and prisoners alike will vanish beneath the sea. Rosalind must choose: flee with the proof or go back for Mateo. Emotional beat: the theme made flesh—love against duty, with minutes on the clock.

chapters.title: The Long Way Up
chapters.summary: Sam's POV. Rosalind goes back. Against decompression limits and flooding compartments, she frees Mateo and two survey survivors while Sam rigs the archive data to broadcast automatically if their ship sinks. Emotional beat: desperate, breathless hope; love choosing its answer.

chapters.title: Surface Fire
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. On the surface, Hale's frigate opens fire on their ship. Priya turns the salvage vessel into a shield, buying time, taking damage. Emotional beat: defiance; ordinary people weaponizing courage against institutional power.

chapters.title: What It Found
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Climax. Cornered and burning, Rosalind triggers the broadcast, then confronts Hale face to face, offering him the same choice he offered her: truth or ruin. His own officers, seeing the evidence stream, stand down. Emotional beat: catharsis—power's corruption undone by exposure, not violence.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Aftermath ashore: inquiries opened, arrests made, the missing team coming home. Rosalind gives her real name publicly for the first time in twelve years, surrendering her old crime alongside the new evidence. Emotional beat: bittersweet release; justice outside the law finally entering it.

chapters.title: Measuring in Years
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV, epilogue. Months later, Rosalind and her crew refit the ship for honest work. Lena sends postcards; Mateo stays aboard. Rosalind stops counting miles and starts counting seasons. Emotional beat: quiet peace—love, once risked, becomes the thing she builds her life around.
